Connect

Hybrid and multi-VPC networking

Connect on-premises networks to AWS, and AWS VPCs to each other.

1. Core Concept

  • Connecting networks requires managing routes and encryption. Peering connects two VPCs directly. Transit Gateway acts as a central hub. Direct Connect provides a physical, private fiber line.

2. Key Services & Features

  • VPC Peering:
    • Direct 1-to-1 connection.
    • Not transitive (A connected to B, and B to C, does NOT connect A to C).
    • CIDR blocks cannot overlap.
  • Transit Gateway:
    • Hub-and-spoke routing architecture.
    • Connects thousands of VPCs and VPNs.
    • Supports transitive routing and multicast.
  • Site-to-Site VPN:
    • Encrypted IPsec tunnel over the public internet.
    • Fast to set up, but bandwidth and latency are subject to internet weather.
  • Direct Connect (DX):
    • Private physical fiber connection.
    • Takes weeks to provision.
    • Not encrypted by default (requires VPN over DX or MACsec).

3. Architecture Rules

  • Use Transit Gateway when you have more than a handful of VPCs to avoid a complex full-mesh peering nightmare.
  • For strict compliance requiring encryption over a private line, run a Site-to-Site VPN over a Direct Connect connection.

4. Scenarios & Use Cases

  • A company requires consistent, predictable 10 Gbps throughput to their data center.
    • Choose: AWS Direct Connect.
    • Why: VPNs traverse the public internet and cannot guarantee consistent high bandwidth.
  • You have 50 VPCs that all need to share a central security inspection VPC.
    • Choose: Transit Gateway.
    • Why: It provides centralized, transitive routing out of the box.

Q1 You have multiple VPN connections and want to provide secure communication between sites using the AWS VPN CloudHub. Which statement is the most accurate in describing what you must do to set this up correctly?

  • B Create a virtual private gateway with multiple customer gateways, each with a unique set of keys.
  • C Create a virtual public gateway with multiple customer gateways, each with a unique Private subnet.
  • D Create a virtual private gateway with multiple customer gateways, each with unique subnet id.

Q36 A company has a centralized networking account and wants to share VPC subnets with multiple application accounts without duplicating VPC infrastructure. Which AWS service enables this?
  • A VPC Peering
  • B AWS Transit Gateway
  • C AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM)
  • D AWS PrivateLink
Answer: C

- **AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM)** allows sharing resources across accounts - Can share VPC subnets between accounts - Resources remain in owner account, but accessible to shared accounts - No need to duplicate VPCs - VPC Peering (A) connects VPCs but doesn't share subnets - Transit Gateway (B) connects networks but doesn't share subnets - PrivateLink (D) is for service-to-VPC connectivity **Benefits of Subnet Sharing with RAM:** - ✅ Centralized network management - ✅ Reduced VPC sprawl - ✅ Efficient IP address usage - ✅ Simplified network architecture - ✅ Lower operational overhead **Other Shareable Resources via RAM:** - VPC Subnets (most common) - Transit Gateway attachments - Route 53 Resolver rules - License Manager configurations - Aurora DB clusters - Prefix lists
